key_insight: In an adversarial time-domain eddy-current example, gauge-penalized H¹ elements can converge to an incorrect state, while mixed H¹/H(Curl) scalar/edge elements yield reasonable results.
engineering_relevance: Electromagnetic finite-element predictions can remain unreliable despite mesh refinement if the discretization does not respect Maxwell’s differential structure.
method: Summarize the mathematical distinctions between H¹ and H(Curl) elements.
Construct a physically feasible, adversarial time-domain eddy-current problem.
Compare gauge-penalized H¹ and gauge-free mixed scalar/edge a–φ formulations.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports failure of penalized H¹ elements even under mesh refinement, contrasted with reasonable results from the mixed scalar/edge formulation.
watch_item: The abstract provides no quantitative error metrics, and the adversarial example does not establish failure for every H¹-based simulation.
paper_title: A time-domain adversarial example demonstrating the failure of $H^1$ elements in $a$-$φ$ electromagnetic simulation
